tl;dr:
Mass Effect: Andromeda (MEA) both is and is not a Mass Effect game. In 71h of single-player content, I encountered very little bugs but very many glitches. For a on-sale price of 10€ (10$) that's excellent!

I think the largest source of discontent with MEA (apart from a botched launch, true to EA's modus operandi) is that it really isn't a fourth part of the epic Original Trilogy (OT). Instead, MEA is its own thing: a game set in the Mass Effect universe, yet afar from the trilogy both in story and in style. 

The Gameplay:
At the core of the gameplay, MEA is a lot like the OT. Shooting guns in third person is fun, as is using your Biotic/Tech/Combat abilities. The hovering jets were a nice addition, though ultimately not that useful IMHO.
Killing enemies gives XP, which can be used to get new abilities. Those are divided into Combat, Biotic and Tech, all of which boil down to Space Magic. All abilities can be upgraded by six levels, the last three of which have a dual choice. Same goes for Squadmates, though they only each have their three abilities plus three attributes. I was a bit annoyed by the limitation to three abilities for Ryder, though one can get more by switching Profiles (like RPG classes) on the fly.
Ryder can scan technology, enemies, and plants to get Research Points, which in turn can be used to develop new weapons, armour, etc.. I found this a better source of new equipment than looting enemies or buying at stores.
Driving around in the Nomad (MEA's equivalent to the OT's Mako) was okay, though not that fun until it was properly upgraded. The Nomad definitely lacks the guns and turret of the Mako, and the low-powered jumpjets weren't all that useful. It was fairly slow as well. 
The space exploration feature was okay, though rudimentary compared to the OT, just flying to a planet, scanning for anomalies, clicking the anomaly, and getting a reward. Meh.

The Story:
71h to complete all main missions, sidequests, and Loyalty missions; that's a lot! There're also a bunch of additional Tasks which I didn't complete, mostly because they necessitate combing through the various maps. 
Quality-wise, the story is okay. It gets its job done but never reached the thrill of the OT. The main missions and Loyalty missions were well executed, though I found the final mission a bit... campy? (*cough* ME2 *cough*)
Some of the sidequests were nice as well but mostly RPG-typic.
There's much lore, from planetary descriptions to readable messages; nice but not breathtaking. I'm not entirely sure how well it fits in with the OT.
Conversations were comparable to the OT, with the well-known six-option wheel to select your choice reply. I was a bit annoyed that unlike the OT things were often black and white. In the OT, you could usually mediate during arguments and find a compromise. In MEA, you had to choose sides, both of which were obviously one-sided. 
Also, there's no Paragon/Renegade system. Instead, there're very few Quicktime Events, some of which make good things happen, some bad. I didn't much like that. One has to choose Ryder's singular personality trait at the beginning, but ultimately it only changes the tone of her replies and is often at odds with the atmosphere.

The Characters:
I... didn't really warm up to them. They feel a bit like fanfiction versions of the OT's characters: the asari scientist, the old krogan battlemaster, the turian rogue, etc.. Sure, they played around with the genders a bit, and everybody's got their own quirks, but it still feels like just copying a school assignment and putting in your own mistakes so the teacher doesn't notice. 
Also, why no equivalent for Tali? We get a not-Liara and a not-Garrus and a not-Wrex and a not-Kaidan and a not-Ashley, but no not-Tali? C'mon, guys!
Same goes for Ryder; (s)he's just not all that likeable. I was a bit surprised at the odd choice of customization: ten faces and hairstyles (with kind of weird hair physics), many colour options, lots of sliders for lips/eyes/chin/..., tons of makeup choices. And, like, four outfits? Not that I want to play dress up; this is not a Sims game. But why so incredibly many makeup options and so little outfit options? It just struck me as odd.

The Level Design:
Loved it! The Galaxy Map (Cluster Map?) is the same semi-open world we know from the OT: new systems unlock with each completed main mission, but you can go whereever you want in the meantime. There are a few hub areas, where you can "only" run around and talk to people, one of which basically is a copy of the Citadel, and one of which is basically a copy of Omega. I found these two a bit uninspired but loved the third one (Aya).
There're a few massive levels where you can drive around in the Nomad or walk on foot. While three of those are basically deserts (rock, ice, sand), I was still surprised at how many things there were to find. 
One additional location was Nomad-only; leaving your trusty tank-car was lethal. This one was pretty barren and also comparably small. It had low gravity, so driving around was pretty fun, though.
And another location was foot-only, with no Nomad available. It was pretty big and very lush. Lovely place, save for the homicidal wildlife. 
But, yeah, I liked the level design a lot. It looked nice, had a lot of stuff to encounter, and good atmosphere!

The Production Value:
The graphics are lovely but for the human and asari characters. The soundtrack was solid but not all that memorable. Voice acting is excellent, with a lot of fantastic Squad Banter when driving/running around. Seriously, I had the same squadmates with me most of the time but still got enough unique dialogue to fill 71h! It's obvious that a lot of love and effort went into some aspects of the game!

Bugs:
The most annoying bug I had was that I couldn't return to proper fullscreen after Alt-Tabbing out of the game. The game hung up twice over the 71h, both times in travel cutscenes. I had no CtDs at all. Twice, an event wasn't properly triggered. Once I had horrible stuttering. All of these were fixed by restarting the game. That's it. 
The glitches, though; those are abundant. Faces look weird, especially Ryder's expressions in dialogue. NPCs teleport in at scene beginnings, some animations come right from the Ministry of Funny Walks, there's a lot of clipping, shadows pop in and out, all asari look pretty darn weird, salarians are freakishly tall, turian mouths are weird, Ryder always exits the Tempest without a helmet but suddenly has a helmet on when gameplay seamlessly starts... I guess EA saved the money for the finaly QA round.

Further Grievances:
MEA features humans, asari, turians, salarians, and krogan, plus the new angara, kett and Remnant. The other races (quarians, elcor, volus, hanar, drell) would've arrived on the Quarian Arc (cancelled DLC?). I find that incredibly disappointing, and it doesn't even make sense (the volus are a turian client race, and the quarians were basically vagrants, not an Arc-launching civilization). 
We don't learn until late in the game when MEA is set in regard to the OT (or, more clearly, if the Arcs left before or after the Reaper invasion). There're a few nods here and there, and when things finally get cleared up, most of those nods don't fit any more.
Origin is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ piece of software. I don't much like Steam either, but at least it's not as useless as Origin. 

Modding:
I used Kahmu's 'Mod Manager Tutorial and my Recommended Mod List' on NexusMods, installing about fifty mods via the Frosty Mod Manager, most of which are cosmetic or change the balancing. It's a bit finicky because MEA doesn't start unless Origin is shut off - if Origin is already started before Steam attempts to start Origin, the game didn't start.
